analysis_notes.format_note: Long-form 16:9 (10:47) second-person 'What if' narrative explainer. Flat 2D vector animation (Jaiden/'stickman with black ball head' style: black circular heads with white expressive eyes, blue hoodie protagonist), single male AI-sounding/neutral narrator, light background music. No burned-in subtitles; on-screen text is limited to glowing money tags above heads, location supers and occasional label chips. Thumbnail is a painterly AI-style illustration that does NOT match the in-video flat style (only the hero's black head + hoodie carry over).
analysis_notes.description_hook: Description restates the premise + a closing moral dilemma question ('Would you use this power to get rich, or change someone's life?').

title_pattern.template: What If You Could See Everyone's [HIDDEN NUMERIC ATTRIBUTE]?
title_pattern.notes: Classic what-if superpower premise framed in second person ('You'). The hidden attribute (future wealth) is universally relatable, implies a visible number per person (perfect for visuals), and immediately suggests a social/moral twist. 9 words, no caps-lock, no number in the title; the giant number lives in the thumbnail instead. Siblings: '...Everyone's Lifespan / Death Date / IQ / Body Count / Remaining Luck'.

thumbnail.composition: Wide street scene split left/right. Left third: hero (black ball head, side-eye, yellow hoodie, backpack, white sneakers) walking past. Right half: an old bearded homeless man sitting on cardboard against a dark wall, palm out, looking up. Glowing price tags with down-pointing triangles float above each head.
thumbnail.text: '$150' (small, blue glow) above the hero; '$8,742,619,300' (huge, neon green glow, ~40% of frame width) above the homeless man. No title text.
thumbnail.colours: Warm golden-hour backlight on the left (orange/amber), dark slate wall on the right; saturated yellow hoodie and neon green number pop against the dark wall; blue vs green tag colour coding.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Status inversion: the poorest-looking person carries the biggest number, the 'normal' kid carries a tiny one. Number size itself encodes the contrast (small $150 vs a 13-character billions figure). The homeless man is rendered more realistically/detailed than the stylised hero.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Instant curiosity gap readable in <1 s without words: 'why does the homeless guy have $8.7 billion?' The exact, oddly specific figure feels like real data. Glowing HUD tags look like a game overlay = 'superpower' visual shorthand. Note the thumb is a richer painterly render than the flat video; the hero's black head keeps brand continuity. The same exact number is the first shot's payoff in the video (thumbnail promise delivered at 0:08).

hook.verbatim_0_5s: "Sir, you dropped this." You bend down to pick up a $5 bill. The homeless man turns around, and that's when you see it, floating above his head.
hook.verbatim_5_15s: $8,742,619,300. $8 billion. You blink, look at his ripped shoes, his cardboard sign, the half-eaten sandwich sitting beside him, then back at the number.
hook.device: Cold open in medias res with a line of dialogue, second-person POV ('you'), and an immediate visual payoff of the thumbnail promise (the exact thumbnail number appears at ~0:08 and is shown full-screen at 0:14). Then contrast stacking (ripped shoes, cardboard sign, half sandwich vs $8B), a self-deprecating comparison (your own number $43,217 at 0:27), and an explicit open loop + foreshadowing at 0:38-0:45: 'You have absolutely no idea what these numbers mean. And by the end of the week, you're going to wish you never found out.' Then a time rewind ('this morning, something very strange happened') to start the chronological story.

beats.summary: 'Sir, you dropped this' - $5 bill, homeless man, $8,742,619,300 appears above his head; thumbnail number delivered.
Ripped shoes / cardboard sign / half sandwich vs $8B; you check your own reflection: $43,217. Joke: he'll be richer than you by ~$8B (full-screen 'Daniel is richer by $8,742,576,083').
'No idea what these numbers mean... by the end of the week you'll wish you never found out.'
Rewind to this morning: mom $286,400, dad $91,200, dog nothing (joke); Google search 'why am I seeing floating numbers'; 'Thanks, Google.'
Street: everyone has a number - mailman $312k, jogger $1.4M, guy yelling at parking meter $27. Clue: Lamborghini neighbour $0, newspaper teen $16M.
It clicks: future wealth = highest net worth they'll ever reach (net-worth curve graphic with peak marked 'Highest net worth ever'). 'Most valuable superpower in human history.'
Goal: get rich. Mall: businessman $140k, janitor $3.2M - interrogation gag ('Kid, I'm trying to clean the floor'); 7-year-old bracelet seller $92M - 'She says she likes purple.'
New plan: don't learn how, just find someone who will. 3 days of watching numbers, notes card (Mailman $312K, Jogger $1.4M, Janitor $3.2M, Girl (purple) $92M).
College student in coffee shop: $64.8 billion (number counts up; bar chart vs 'famous billionaires'). 'Just an app.' 'It's always an app.' You understood 12%.
You become his marketing partner; a month of building; daily number check: still 64B.
Investor offers $2M; you read investor $18M vs friend $64.8B and whisper 'Don't take the deal'. Friend rejects. 'Congratulations... Or so you think.'
Number drops $64.8B -> $4.2M. Rule upgrade: numbers are predictions, actions change them (branching-path diagram). 'You may have just destroyed it.' Night of thinking; -$60,000,000,000 tag.
Friend furious, investor was linked to a big tech company, launch in doubt; 'I trusted you' - you're out. Your own number drops $43,217 -> $12,600.
If numbers can change, why did the homeless man still have $8B? Callback to the cold open.
Daniel: construction injury, lost job, eviction, years lost; estranged daughter, old photograph. 'She thinks I abandoned her.' Shift: you stop thinking about money.
You help Daniel, search 2 days, find daughter (26, medical research lab) - SAME exact number $8,742,619,300 'to the dollar'.
Reunion hug; Daniel's number drops $8.7B -> $86,000 while hers stays.

Numbers = highest wealth on current path. Without the reunion she'd quit her research; her fortune would have passed to Daniel via her will after her death ('Last will... goes to my father, Daniel'). Now a new path.
He has no idea what he lost and couldn't look happier. Your number: still $12,600. 'Maybe you're just terrible at this superpower.'
Man in suit with $0 above head; distracted truck driver; realization: the number is also about TIME (death = $0). 'LOOK OUT!' - truck swerves; $0 -> $2,800,000. You saved his life.
Every number is a future that hasn't happened yet; billionaire may lose everything, homeless man may get rich, a $0 stranger may just need a warning.
Walking home your number ticks up $1 at a time: $12,600 -> 12,601 -> 12,602. 'Investing in something that matters... people.'
'If you could see exactly how rich everyone would become, would you use it to make yourself wealthy? Or would you change someone's future...?' end card text.

pacing.notes: Fastest cutting in the comedic exploitation/cafe acts (min 3-5, ~30 cuts/min); slows during the emotional Daniel backstory (min 7, 12 cuts/min). Narration is wall-to-wall with short punchy sentences and frequent one-line deadpan jokes.

techniques_worth_copying: One visual mechanic carries the whole video: a glowing tag above every head. Each new character = a new number = a micro-reveal. Cheap to produce, endlessly reusable.
Numbers as characters: exact, oddly specific figures ($8,742,619,300, $43,217, $27) feel concrete and funny; full-screen number cards with a spelled-out label for the big ones.
Second-person 'you' protagonist - the viewer is the hero, so no voice acting or character intro needed.
Thumbnail number reused verbatim as the first reveal (promise paid in 8 s).

Escalating rule system: rule 1 (numbers = future wealth) -> rule 2 (they're predictions; actions change them) -> rule 3 (highest on CURRENT path) -> rule 4 (also about time/death). Each rule reveal is a twist that re-hooks and recontextualises earlier scenes.
Mystery set up in the cold open (why does the homeless man have $8B?) parked at 0:45 and paid off at 7:30-8:40 - holds viewers to the 2/3 mark.

Deadpan comedy beats every 15-20 s in Act 1-2 (dog has no financial future; 'Thanks, Google'; 'She says she likes purple'; 'It's always an app'; 'You understood 12%') then a tonal shift to sincerity (Daniel) for the emotional payoff.
Greedy-plan backfires -> moral turn arc; ends on a small earned reward (number ticking up $1 at a time) and a two-sided moral question for comments.
Explain abstract rules with clean navy-background motion graphics (line charts, branching paths, bar charts) between story scenes.
Label chips (NOT GUARANTEED, HEALTHY, MESSY HAIR, UNDERSTOOD: 12%) as visual punchlines instead of subtitles.
Status-inversion cast: homeless man / janitor / 7-year-old / paperboy get huge numbers; Lamborghini owner / suited man get $0.

code_only_remake_needs.feasibility: Very high - the in-video style is already flat vector and almost entirely reproducible in Remotion/SVG. Only the painterly thumbnail would need a stylised SVG equivalent.
code_only_remake_needs.characters: SVG rig: black circle head with white almond eyes + eyebrows (expression set: neutral, side-eye, shock O-mouth, smug, sad, crying, determined), stick limbs in coloured hoodie/jacket body shapes, accessories (beanie, glasses, afro, cap, lab coat, suit+tie). Walk/run cycle, sit, point, shrug, hand-to-head poses. Gloved hand + object insert component.
code_only_remake_needs.environments: ~8 reusable flat backgrounds: shop-street with storefront signs (bank, electronics with chart screen, cafe awning), crosswalk at day/night, mall storefront row, kitchen, bedroom, coffee shop interior, park with hedges/bench, lab. Parallax layers + gaussian background blur for close-ups (depth-of-field look).
code_only_remake_needs.money_tag_component: Rounded dark pill with glowing coloured text and down-pointer, anchored above a character head; props: value, colour (green/white/red), animate modes = pop-in, count-up/roll, flip/glitch change between values, tick +$1.
code_only_remake_needs.graphics: Full-screen number card (navy gradient, small caps label + big glowing number, counter roll), line chart draw-on with highlighted peak, branching-path diagram, bar chart, network nodes diagram, handwritten note/letter cards (handwriting font), phone search UI, calendar with X's, label chips.
code_only_remake_needs.camera: Hard cuts every ~2 s between wide / medium / close-up of the same scene (just re-framing one SVG scene at different scale + blur), slow push-ins on reactions, snap zoom on tag changes, iris wipe, split-screen.
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Single TTS narrator (Kokoro) at ~165 wpm, light ambient music bed, whoosh/ding SFX on number reveals, cash-register/counter SFX on count-ups.
code_only_remake_needs.data: Storyboard JSON per shot: scene id, framing preset, characters + expression + pose, tags with values, chips, text cards. Word-timed TTS to align reveals with the spoken number.
